title: Exact polynomial byte-region contract
objective: Specify and differentially verify a direct signed byte-region ingress and egress contract for packed ZZ[x] and QQ[x] coefficients, with implementation-ready ABI and measured current overhead

handoff.summary: Defined an implementation-ready, storage-neutral SJPZ/SJPQ v1 byte-region contract without changing shared FFI or public polynomial code. The ordinary Python oracle normalizes encoder input, strictly validates selected offset/length ranges, signed magnitudes, reduced rational pairs, zero and trailing-zero rules, caller-supplied platform coefficient limits, and constructs results transactionally. CPython and Sage.js witnesses pass by default; the same witness passed SageMath 10.9.post30 with SAGEJS_SAGE_ORACLE=/home/user/sagelite/sage. Current generated FLINT egress is byte-for-byte identical. The later ABI reuses FlintByteRegion.from_bytes and adds non-consuming fmpz/fmpq_polynomial_from_byte_region(region, offset, length) resource constructors. On Node this admits one literal host-to-owned-region copy; Wasm instead has one host-boundary copy plus owned-region materialization. Warm linux-x64 measurements show the current bytes-to-BigInt stage at 8.4 ms for 0.5 MB dense ZZ, 12.5 ms for 1 MB dense QQ, and 12.8 ms for one 1 MB skewed coefficient, versus 0.11, 0.13, and 0.10 ms for the Node byte-region copy. Current deserialization takes another 2.3, 8.5, and 19.6 ms, but those measurements combine avoidable transport reconstruction with unavoidable parse/import work and do not measure the future parser. Egress is already efficient and remains unchanged.
risks: This lane specifies and tests the contract but deliberately does not implement the native primitive; sanitizer, lifecycle, Node, and Wasm proof belongs to the later shared-FFI lane.

The exact polynomial resources currently declare wasm=False. The byte-region resource and synchronous borrowed model are conceptually Wasm-capable, but exact polynomial resource lowering and its host-boundary-copy plus owned-region-materialization lifecycle must be implemented and verified separately.

Dense QQ construction remains dominated by rational coercion and numerator/denominator extraction (about 163 ms for 100000 small coefficients here). The measured 12.5 ms bytes-to-BigInt stage is avoidable; the additional 8.5 ms current deserializer combines avoidable byte reconstruction with unavoidable FLINT parse/import work, so the future parser's total speedup remains unmeasured.

A full pnpm test:native run is recorded as an inherited failure: after 437 seconds it reached test/native-kernel.cjs:1042 and found the source_include_dirs fmpq_matrix_ffi.h where the base test expected its copied temporary-prefix header. A separate extension lane reproduced the same shared-base issue. The first attempt also exposed that the parallel native cache does not provision M4RI; building packages/m4ri locally allowed the suite to proceed. Neither failure involves files claimed here.
next_steps: Refactor the existing exact-polynomial parser helpers to read const unsigned char ranges directly, construct a temporary sealed resource, and publish it only after full validation; do not reconstruct a ulong stream from fmpz transport.

Declare fmpz_polynomial_from_byte_region and fmpq_polynomial_from_byte_region using the existing FlintByteRegion argument plus checked uint64 offset/length, Status(1, exception=ValueError, ...), non-consuming ownership, target size_t/slong/WORD_MAX count checks, and explicit Node/Wasm capability metadata.

Change public exact construction and SagePack restore to create one FlintByteRegion from the canonical Uint8Array, call the resource constructor, and close the byte region in finally; then delete the bytes-to-hex-to-BigInt helper and old payload:fmpz_t deserializers under the greenfield rule.

Differentially fuzz the new native parser against this oracle, add ASan/UBSan lifecycle coverage, prove malformed calls leave no result and do not consume the region, and rerun this benchmark plus the public construction benchmarks.
Optimize QQ coefficient coercion/extraction independently after the byte boundary is fixed; it is now the larger measured cost for dense small rational coefficients.
